item.title: On this machine
item.description:
A secret is a value. A name, a {{placeholder}}, and a vault reference are not. The app stores the value in the OS keychain and keeps the name in the file you might commit.

flowchart LR
 field["A secret field"]:::step
 ref{"akv:// or op://?"}:::gate
 vault[("Vault")]:::secret
 chain[("OS keychain")]:::store
 sent["The call"]:::out

 field --> ref
 ref --> vault --> sent
 ref --> chain --> sent

 classDef store fill:#134e4a,stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef secret fill:#FFC131,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:2px,color:#1a1404
 classDef gate fill:#FFC131,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:2px,color:#1a1404
 classDef step fill:#0f766e,stroke:#99f6e4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef out fill:#155e75,stroke:#67e8f9,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 linkStyle 0 stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 1,2 stroke:#FFC131,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 3,4 stroke:#67e8f9,stroke-width:2.5px

The keychain link

API keys, bearer tokens, basic passwords, client secrets, the OpenAI key, the MCP Azure client secret, and stdio env values whose names look like secrets use the OS keychain. The service name is termorq.
